subject: QuickLink integration — revenue waterfall, lead ownership, and commercial scope
messages:
From: Alex Rivers <alex@quicklink.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@quicklink.io>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuickLink x Redwood — commercial model and lead registration

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — QuickLink's integrations team is excited about shipping a connector to Redwood's hosted API. Before our technical kickoff, procurement asked me to put the commercial outline on the table so legal and finance can review in parallel.

High-level asks from our side:
- Simple referral + reseller paths for the connector (we'd like the option to resell to a subset of our customers).
- Clear lead registration window (we typically request 120 days lookback for inbound registrations).
- A standard rev-share for co-sell: 20% of Redwood net ARR for leads we bring that convert during the pilot / first-year.

I've attached a short one-pager with our expectations and a draft SOW for the integration. Can we get Redwood's preferred waterfall and any mandatory contract clauses we should expect?

Alex Rivers
Head of Partnerships | QuickLink
[Attachment: QuickLink_Draft_SOW.pdf (PDF)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivers <alex@quicklink.io>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@quicklink.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuickLink x Redwood — commercial model and lead registration

Alex — thanks for the clear outline. Appreciate you sending the SOW.

Quick notes up front:
- We're comfortable with a referral + reseller dual-path approach. For reseller we usually require a minimum onboarding fee and co-marketing commitments; we can surface numbers after a quick pilots economics sync.
- Lead registration: our standard window is 90 days with a 12-month acceleration clause for deals that convert within the year; we can consider 120 days for strategic partners with committed co-sell motion.
- Rev-share: we typically standardize on a waterfall that pays introductory credit on the first-year net ARR (after discounts & credits). 20% is in-range; I'll run that with finance.

I've attached a baseline revshare waterfall we use and a one-page mutual action plan to keep the pilot moving. Can Marissa and Ben loop in legal/partner-ops items we should flag?

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic Partners | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: revshare-waterfall-sheet.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivers <alex@quicklink.io>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuickLink x Redwood — commercial model and lead registration

Adding a few legal/ops questions so we can produce a clean MSAs + SOW combo: 

1) Clawbacks and churn treatment — what triggers a clawback on paid credits? We typically propose a 90-day clawback window tied to customer cancellations where revenue is fully refunded.
2) Lead registration proof — QuickLink will need a simple required field list (lead source, date, sales contact, contact email) plus minimum engagement evidence.
3) Reseller discounting — do you expect margin protection? If QuickLink will resell, we need to bake in a MAP discount schedule so refunds/credits don't create negative-margin flows.
4) Reporting cadence — to pay rev-share we need monthly invoicing and a quarterly reconciliation window.

Camila, can you confirm the SRE/technical kickoff availability? Ben, if you have a standard reseller clause, paste it inline or attach.

Marissa Cole
Director, Partner GTM | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: revshare-waterfall-sheet.xlsx (version 2) (XLSX)]

From: Alex Rivers <alex@quicklink.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuickLink x Redwood — commercial model and lead registration

Marissa — thanks, good questions. Answers below: 

1) Clawbacks: we can accept a 90-day clawback tied to full refunds; for churn within year 1 we propose a pro-rata recovery rather than a full clawback.
2) Lead proof: we'll provide CRM exports, demo logs, and the initial discovery email trail when requested. 120-day window is important to QuickLink because our sales cycles vary.
3) Reseller margin: we can accept a MAP discount schedule — QuickLink requests a minimum 25% margin to make reselling viable.
4) Reporting: monthly statements are fine; we'd like automated CSV exports from your billing system into our finance pipeline.

I've uploaded QuickLink's procurement contact to loop in once terms look close. Also attaching our internal reseller clause for legal review.

Alex Rivers
Head of Partnerships | QuickLink
[Attachment: QL_Draft_Redealer_Clause.docx (DOCX)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivers <alex@quicklink.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuickLink x Redwood — commercial model and lead registration

Alex / team — see inline redlines and a suggested compromise on a few items: 

- Lead registration window: we can agree to 120 days for pilots if QuickLink commits to a joint pipeline review every 60 days and shares CRM evidence on request.
- Clawback: Redwood will do a 90-day full-clawback; for churn between 90-365 days we'll propose a 6-month pro-rata recovery, capped at the original credit amount.
- Margin & MAP: we won't pre-commit to a fixed margin guarantee; instead we'll include a resell tier in the SOW where QuickLink can choose a standard reseller discount table (options A/B) that balances margin and marketing support.
- Termination & notice: propose 60 days written notice for reseller termination with a 6-month wind-down for active contracts.

I'll attach sample clause language for a 'Lead Protection and Registration' addendum and a short reseller clause excerpt. If these look reasonable we can produce an updated MSA + SOW for signatures.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Lead_Protection_Addendum.txt (TXT)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivers <alex@quicklink.io>, Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@quicklink.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuickLink x Redwood — commercial model and lead registration

Great progress — thanks everyone for the quick turns. Proposed mutual action plan and next steps:

1) Legal: Redwood to send updated MSA + Lead Protection addendum incorporating Ben's redlines by Tue 5/4 — owner: Ben.
2) Commercials: Redwood finance to confirm waterfall math and finalize whether 20% flat or tiered options A/B by Wed 5/5 — owner: Marissa.
3) Procurement: QuickLink to share procurement contact and any purchase order processes — owner: Alex (ASAP).
4) Technical kickoff: schedule week of 5/10; Camila to lead SRE sync and provide sandbox creds — owner: Camila.
5) Pilot: propose a 60-day paid pilot with defined success metrics (50 active seats or $X ARR, whichever triggers expansion) — agreed-in-principle, finalize in SOW.

If you confirm these owners/timeline I'll produce a short tracker and drop it into the HubSpot deal record.

Thanks — Jordan
Account Executive, Strategic Partners | Redwood Inference
